name: Function Sum
description: Suppose you have an integer array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$. Let $$$\operatorname{lsl}(i)$$$ be the number of indices $$$j$$$ ($$$1 \le j \lt i$$$) such that $$$a_j \lt a_i$$$. Analogically, let $$$\operatorname{grr}(i)$$$ be the number of indices $$$j$$$ ($$$i \lt j \le n$$$) such that $$$a_j \gt a_i$$$. Let's name position $$$i$$$ good in the array $$$a$$$ if $$$\operatorname{lsl}(i) \lt \operatorname{grr}(i)$$$. Finally, let's define a function $$$f$$$ on array $$$a$$$ $$$f(a)$$$ as the sum of all $$$a_i$$$ such that $$$i$$$ is good in $$$a$$$. Given two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$, find the sum of $$$f(a)$$$ over all arrays $$$a$$$ of size $$$n$$$ such that $$$1 \leq a_i \leq k$$$ for all $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$ modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
input_specification: The first and only line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 50$$$; $$$2 \leq k \lt 998\,244\,353$$$).
output_specification: Output a single integer — the sum of $$$f$$$ over all arrays $$$a$$$ of size $$$n$$$ modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
approach_summary: Transform coefficient polynomials to point-value form via FFT/NTT in O(N log N). Multiply point values in O(N) and invert back to achieve fast polynomial convolution.
